source_title: @webcontainer/api 1.6.4 (npm registry record)
claim_summary: npm registry records @webcontainer/api 1.6.4 published 2026-04-14T11:25Z, the first non-prerelease since 1.6.1 (2025-04-23); later 1.6.5-internal.1 (2026-04-15) and 1.6.5-internal.2 (2026-07-10) prereleases; registry license field reads MIT
availability: npm stable release; changelog not read
limitation: Registry metadata only; no changelog or functional test. Licence conflict: package metadata says MIT while webcontainers.io/enterprise states a commercial licence is required for production for-profit use of the API

source_title: 7 things Opus 4.7 does better than 4.6
claim_summary: Vendor says Opus 4.7 outperformed Opus 4.6 on its own app-building evals by up to ~10% and solved an internal 'AI-resistant' challenge after 7.5 hours; implies the model is offered in Bolt
feature: third-party model integration and internal evals
limitation: Vendor-internal evaluation with no public denominator, task set or variance; exact availability date and plan scope not stated

source_title: pkg-pr-new npm versions 0.0.67-0.0.91
claim_summary: npm registry lists 21 pkg-pr-new versions in the window, 0.0.67 (2026-04-26) through 0.0.91 (2026-10-07), with a gap between 0.0.75 (2026-05-19) and 0.0.78 (2026-07-13); MIT; GitHub repo stackblitz-labs/pkg.pr.new has tags only, no GitHub releases
feature: continuous preview-package publishing service for open-source PRs
limitation: Release cadence is not adoption or quality; individual changelogs not read; one row summarises a release series

product: Bolt.new for Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365
source_title: Agentic building across the enterprise with Bolt.new on Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365
claim_summary: Vendor announces Azure and Microsoft 365 integration: Bolt.new 'will be available' via Microsoft Marketplace, Azure deployment, Teams invocation, M365 Copilot integration; cites a customer case (12 months to three to four months; seats 50 to nearly 70) and '75% of the Fortune 500'
feature: enterprise cloud deployment and procurement integration
availability: mostly future tense ('will be available', 'will be able')
limitation: Customer outcome and Fortune 500 figures are vendor/customer statements without denominator; no Microsoft-side page was read (Azure surfaces deliberately not accessed); shipping dates not stated

source_title: alien-signals v3.2.0
claim_summary: GitHub release v3.2.0 (2026-05-12T14:05Z) adds effect cleanup functions and four propagation bug fixes, with a breaking-style note for custom createReactiveSystem implementors; npm 3.2.0 (2026-05-12) and 3.2.1 (2026-05-14); MIT
limitation: Library release is not evidence of downstream use; custom implementors must change code (maintenance cost) per release note

source_title: Design in Stitch, build in Bolt
claim_summary: Carries forward 026-E01: vendor says Google Stitch added an 'Export to Bolt' button that hands off layout, components, design tokens and a DESIGN.md file, and that the Stitch update also ships MCP integration
availability: vendor-reported as live; feature sits in Google Stitch
limitation: No Google-side primary source found or read; page modified 2026-08-17 and the earlier report's title 'Export Google Stitch designs to Bolt in one click' does not appear on it; conversion fidelity untested

source_title: @stackblitz/sdk 1.11.1 (npm registry record)
claim_summary: npm records @stackblitz/sdk 1.11.1 on 2026-07-02, the first release since 1.11.0 (2024-07-03); repo commit 2026-07-01 'fix: allow cross-origin-isolation for the run endpoint (#39)'; MIT
limitation: Single maintenance fix; two-year gap suggests low release cadence; no functional test

source_title: Bolt.new was named a notable vendor by Forrester
claim_summary: Vendor says Forrester's 'The Agentic Development Platforms Landscape, Q3 2026' includes Bolt.new as a notable vendor; page carries Forrester's non-endorsement disclaimer
limitation: Forrester report itself not read (gated); inclusion in a landscape is attention, not verified adoption or quality

source_title: Build what you couldn’t imagine before, with Bolt Slides
claim_summary: Vendor launches Bolt Slides, an AI deck builder whose output is a live web app, 'available now to every Bolt.new user, free and paid', and states it is open source and runnable with Claude Code, Codex or Cursor; GitHub stackblitz/bolt-slides created 2026-07-14 (MIT, commit 'Bolt Slides — initial open source release'), 8 commits through 2026-07-30 incl. two merged external PRs
availability: GA to all plans (vendor-reported); MIT repo
limitation: Repo star count is attention not use; no release tags; agent-portability claim not tested

source_title: Introducing Skills: Create your ideal AI builder
claim_summary: Carries forward 026-E02: 'Skills are live now'; reusable bundles of context, rules and actions with a pre-built library, custom skills, upload from other tools or skill repos, and workspace- or project-scoped sharing
limitation: Page modified 2026-08-18; uploaded third-party skills raise provenance/security questions not addressed; no task-level evaluation

source_title: Security belongs in the platform, not in your backlog
claim_summary: Vendor says a free 'Run security audit' step in the publish menu scans a project, applies mechanical fixes automatically and flags architectural ones, takes two to three minutes and does not consume user tokens; cites third-party figures (Veracode 45 percent, Endor Labs 20 to 57 percent, Georgia Tech 74 vulnerabilities)
feature: pre-publish AI security review and auto-fix
limitation: Auto-applied fixes are unreviewed code changes; no false-positive/negative rate or independent test; cited statistics are second-hand and were not checked at their origin

source_title: Issues saving project files
claim_summary: Status record: users unable to save project files 07:29-08:47 UTC, worst status partial outage; vendor linked it to reported Cloudflare network issues and resolved after Cloudflare's resolution
limitation: Only partial-outage entry in the visible history; no postmortem; affected-user share not stated

source_title: Issues publishing projects
claim_summary: Status record: publishing hanging or stuck from 2026-08-06T16:52Z; fix deployed 2026-08-07T18:25Z, resolved 2026-08-07T22:29Z (about 30 hours), worst status degraded performance
limitation: No root cause or postmortem published on the page

source_title: Dictation is live: Bolt.new is ready to listen
claim_summary: Vendor says dictation is live in the prompt box and strips false starts and filler; cites a 2018 study (speech 2.93 times faster than phone typing)
limitation: No accuracy, privacy or audio-retention terms stated in the post; cited study not checked

source_title: Bolt Open Source Fund 2026
claim_summary: Vendor renews its open-source fund: says some 2025 sponsorships were not applied at the time and are being applied now, adds $1,700/month for a new run-rate of $11,333/month, and reports 27 developers in EPD (22 in 2025) for the Open Source Pledge calculation
limitation: Payments not verified on GitHub Sponsors or Open Source Pledge; the post itself discloses that the 2025 plan was only partly executed

source_title: Prompt queueing is live: queue your next idea while Bolt.new builds
claim_summary: Vendor says prompt queueing is live in every project for everyone: reorder/edit/delete queued prompts, retry failures, shared queue for teammates, per-prompt agent choice; queue shows the next five prompts
limitation: Queued prompts each consume usage; no data on failure cascades or cost

source_title: Visual Edits: edit your app by clicking on it
claim_summary: Vendor says Visual Edits, a click-and-change toolbar whose batched changes go to the selected model, is available to all free and paid users as of 2026-09-03; covers text and styling only, no layout moves
limitation: Batch still spends tokens per vendor; no measured reduction in iterations

source_title: What is Bolt Forge?
claim_summary: Carries forward 026-E03: research preview of an open-model agent (GLM 5.3 Flash default; GLM 5.3; Kimi K3 and DeepSeek v4 Pro experimental); up to 50X usage on individual Pro through 2026-10-14; opt-in sharing of de-identified prompts, code, files, tool calls and fix traces into datasets licensed to AI developers starting with Arcee AI (StackBlitz may be paid); Teams/Enterprise and EEA/UK/Switzerland sessions excluded from training; vendor Build Index 92.2 vs 101.0 for Claude Opus 5
limitation: Build Index is vendor-run; de-identification untested; deletion of already-collected data is by email request; a commercial dataset-licensing model is a rights issue for code built in Forge

source_title: Bolt Forge Gives Developers 50x More AI Coding Power for Free
claim_summary: Same-day secondary report restates the Forge terms and notes the Build Index is internal; it also states that Bolt 'promises' to release the resulting model weights openly and that a $9/month Bolt Lite plan launches
limitation: Not independent testing; the open-weights promise was NOT found in the Bolt blog post or the support doc read on 2026-10-16 (conflict recorded, unresolved)

source_title: Bolt.new makes its first acquisition: Dokai
claim_summary: Carries forward 026-E04: Bolt.new (described as 'the StackBlitz platform') announces its first acquisition, Dokai (enterprise go-to-market agents); terms not disclosed; first Dokai-based capabilities for enterprise customers promised for 'late fall'; vendor states roughly half of enterprise customers start building before contract signature and average first deploy within 34 days
limitation: No independent confirmation of the deal or filing; customer metrics are vendor statements without denominator

source_title: Bolt.new status history
claim_summary: Visible status history begins 2026-07-15; through 2026-10-12 (UTC published_at) it lists 170 entries. Independent re-parse of the embedded page JSON on 2026-10-16: 143 automated '[Dependency Check]' mirrors of upstream providers (Cloudflare 50, Anthropic 41, GitHub 24, Name.com 15, Supabase 9, NPM 3, Stackblitz 1) and 27 own entries (20 degraded performance, 4 operational, 1 partial outage, 2 maintenance), the last in-window being 'Features → Prompting  Degraded' (2026-10-12T20:17Z); 'Subscription Updates Intermittently Failing' ran 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-12. The first-pass parse reported 144/26 (Anthropic 42, 19 degraded)
feature: service reliability and third-party dependency exposure
limitation: History before 2026-07-15 not shown, so April-mid July is missing, not zero; dependency mirrors are not Bolt outages; counts depend on our parser of embedded page JSON and differed by one entry between two same-day parses (spot-check re-parse used here); nine own 'Features → Prompting  Degraded' entries carry automated updates

source_title: Release v1.0.1
claim_summary: bolt.diy v1.0.1 published 2026-10-12T16:49Z, the first release since v1.0.0 (2025-05-12); notes list 118 changes (incl. MCP integration, discuss mode, GitHub and Vercel deployment, Electron build fixes) and 12 first-time contributors; repo licence MIT, README says it uses the WebContainers API, which has commercial licensing terms for enterprise deployment
limitation: Change list spans 17 months of merged PRs, not one quarter; no security advisories published for the repo; no functional test
